_comment: Illustrative off-chain view of an ERC-8004 Validation Registry entry (fields mirror contracts/ValidationRegistryUpgradeable.sol: validationRequest(address validatorAddress, uint256 agentId, string requestURI, bytes32 requestHash) + validationResponse(bytes32 requestHash, uint8 response, string responseURI, bytes32 responseHash, string tag)). ELARA supplies the request-side evidence — requestURI + requestHash — which is content-addressed and offline-recomputable. The on-chain identity fields (validatorAddress, agentId) and the validator's response verdict are the registry's side: 'the vector shows the JOIN, their side of the anchor is theirs.' No chain interaction happens on our side.

_meta.requestHash_algorithm: SHA-256 over the raw bytes of the mandate envelope at requestURI. ERC-8004's requestHash is an OPAQUE bytes32 mapping key — the registry never recomputes or interprets it on-chain — so any collision-resistant 32-byte digest serves. We use SHA-256 because it is the same content-address this demo's x402 settlement receipt back-links to (envelope attestationDigest), so one published envelope anchors both registries. An implementer preferring Ethereum-native keccak256 swaps one hash call; the JOIN pattern is identical.

_response_note: response/responseHash are validator-supplied and shown illustratively (response is a validator-defined uint8; 100 used here for a fully-valid verdict). Elara's offline verdict is DETERMINISTIC — the signing-incapable verifier returns CONSISTENT/authorized or NOT-AUTHORIZED with no scoring model — so a validator running Elara can set responseHash to the content-address of that verdict and any third party recomputes it by re-running the verify command. responseHash is left null here rather than pinning a hash of human-rendered text (which would couple this vector to the verifier's output formatting).
